tools.name: noaa_find_grid
tools.description: Which PRF grids are at a place: the 0.25-degree grid holding a point (latitude and longitude, with neighbors: true for the up to 8 around it), the grids RMA places in a county (county and state), or details for grid IDs. Each grid comes with its bounds and center, whether NCEI has its latest final monthly value (not general data coverage), and the counties RMA places it in (name, state, 5-digit FIPS) from the current crop year's PRF actuarial data (the newest bundled when it isn't); a point also gets its subgrid (sub_id). Use first when the user gives a place instead of a grid ID; a city or address goes in as its coordinates. Then pass the grid IDs to the other tools. Example: {"latitude": 38.25, "longitude": -99.5}

grid_ids.description: 1-20 grid IDs, e.g. [26516, 26517]. Or give latitude and longitude, or county and state, instead.

anyOf.description: 0.25-degree grid ID, e.g. 26516. Get one from latitude/longitude with noaa_find_grid.

items.description: Grid ID: a number for CONUS (e.g. 26516) or a Hawaii ID string (e.g. "H0319").

longitude.description: Longitude in decimal degrees, negative west, e.g. -99.5.

neighbors.description: With latitude/longitude: also the up to 8 grids around the point's grid.

county.description: With state: every PRF grid in the county. Name ("Jefferson"), 3-digit county code ("087") or 5-digit FIPS ("20087").

state.description: With county: the county's state. Name ("Kansas"), postal code ("KS") or FIPS code ("20").

tools.name: noaa_get_precipitation
tools.description: How much precipitation have these grids had? By default, per grid: the current month so far and the last 3 completed months, each beside its NCEI normal (mm and inches) and percent of normal, with its stage (only final is final; initial, synced and unsynced are preliminary); the crop year (January on) to date against normal; and one line on whether it is running wet or dry. Give a place: grid_ids (1-20), latitude and longitude (neighbors: true adds the grids around the point), or county and state. On request: start_month/end_month for another span (at most 24 months), granularity "daily" for daily values and stats (at most 3 months), source "cpc" (the data RMA used before; normals are NCEI-only) or "both" (side by side with the difference). For the PRF index use noaa_get_grid_index; for where in the grid it fell use noaa_get_subgrid_precipitation. Example: {"grid_ids": [26516]}

tools.name: noaa_get_subgrid_precipitation
tools.description: Where inside the grid did the precipitation fall? By default, per grid, the latest completed month: each 1/24-degree subgrid (up to 36 per grid) beside its own normal and percent of it, the grid against normal, the driest and wettest subgrids, subgrids far from the rest, and gauge density (SPARSE or unknown means too few gauges for subgrid detail). Amounts in mm and inches; only stage final is final. Give a place for 1-5 grids: grid_ids, latitude and longitude, or county and state. NCEI only. On request: month (YYYY-MM; this month for the month so far), or interval (1-11, 1 = Jan-Feb ... 11 = Nov-Dec, or RMA's code 625-635) with year (default this year); sub_id for one subgrid; daily: true for each subgrid's daily values. For grid totals over months use noaa_get_precipitation. Example: {"grid_ids": [26516], "interval": 5, "year": 2025}

tools.name: noaa_track_interval
tools.description: Where the PRF interval in progress is heading for 1-20 grids: precipitation so far beside the average to date (mm and inches), the latest days' pace, the index if no more precipitation falls, the projected index p10/p50/p90 and the chance of finishing below each coverage level (70-90) with the base years they rest on, each labeled final or estimate with data_through. Give a place: grid_ids, latitude and longitude (neighbors: true adds the grids around it), or county and state. interval: 1-11 (1 = Jan-Feb ... 11 = Nov-Dec) or RMA's code 625-635, default the interval ending this month; coverage_level adds the chance it pays and the expected payment factor; sub_id (one grid only) tracks one subgrid against its own normal; daily: true lists each day beside its average. For a whole crop year's policy use noaa_policy_outlook; for past years' indexes noaa_get_grid_index. Example: {"grid_ids": [26516], "interval": 9, "coverage_level": 85}

tools.name: noaa_policy_outlook
tools.description: Will my PRF policy pay this crop year, or will I get rained out? For 1-20 grids and the crop year (2027 on; default the current one), each insured interval's average, precipitation so far beside it (mm and inches), its index labeled published (RMA's final index, what RMA pays on), final (computed RMA's way from NCEI's final months, before RMA publishes) or estimate (a month still preliminary), and for intervals still open the chance of finishing below each coverage level, from the projection of an interval in progress (with the base years it rests on) or the grid's past 30 years. Give a place: grid_ids, latitude and longitude (neighbors: true adds the grids around it), or county and state. More coverage gives more: coverage_level (70, 75, 80, 85, 90) adds pays or not, payment factor and chance it pays; intervals (1-11 or RMA's codes 625-635, 625 = Jan-Feb ... 635 = Nov-Dec) with percent of value (at least 2, summing to 100) add the policy's combined odds, break-even and verdict (not_started, paid, paid_below_premium, on_track_to_pay, uncertain, likely_rained_out, rained_out); acres (and county when a grid spans counties; units for per-grid detail) add RMA's dollars: protection, producer premium, indemnity earned and expected, net. Use noaa_track_interval for day-by-day detail on one interval in progress, and noaa_policy_history for how this coverage did in past years. RMA's Actuarial Information Browser is the authority for actual indemnities. Example: {"grid_ids": [26516], "coverage_level": 85, "intervals": [{"interval": 628, "percent": 50}, {"interval": 634, "percent": 50}], "acres": 640}

tools.name: noaa_get_data_status
tools.description: Check how current the data is: NCEI's latest final and initial month and daily file, CPC's latest day, the RMA crop-year index files in use (bundled or downloaded), the averages tables installed per NCEI crop year, the PRF actuarial data bundled per crop year (with the date of RMA's Actuarial Data Master it came from), and whether subgrid normals are installed. Takes no place. Use when data may be missing or to check freshness. Saves a local snapshot and reports changes since the previous check. Example: {}.

tools.name: noaa_policy_history
tools.description: How would this PRF Rainfall Index coverage have done in past years? Scores every past year in RMA's NCEI index file for the crop year (each year against that crop year's average) per grid and interval: median index, p10/p90, trend per decade, driest and wettest year, and the years below each coverage level. Give more of the coverage for more: coverage_level (70, 75, 80, 85 or 90) for that level only; intervals with percent of value for each year's combined payment factor (payment per dollar of protection), years paid, best and worst year; acres too for indemnity, producer premium and net per year, priced at the crop year's county base value and premium rates for every year. Default: the newest 20 years; years {start, end} or a count for others, at most 30. Crop years 2027 on (NCEI). Place: grid_ids (1-20), latitude and longitude (neighbors adds the grids around), or county and state. Intervals 1-11 (1 = Jan-Feb ... 11 = Nov-Dec) or RMA's codes 625-635. Use noaa_policy_outlook for this crop year, noaa_get_grid_index for each year's index. These are estimates under today's rules, not what was paid: RMA's Actuarial Information Browser is the authority for actual indemnities. Example: {"grid_ids": [26516], "coverage_level": 90, "intervals": [{"interval": 628, "percent": 50}, {"interval": 634, "percent": 50}], "acres": 500}

tools.name: noaa_get_grid_index
tools.description: What was the PRF Rainfall Index for these grids in these years? Returns RMA's published index (% of average) per interval and year, beside the interval's precipitation and its average (mm and inches). Requires years: {start, end} or a count of the newest years, at most 30 per grid. Use noaa_policy_history for statistics (how often it paid, median, trend), noaa_compare_sources for how NCEI changed a grid against CPC. Place: grid_ids (1-20), latitude and longitude (neighbors adds the grids around), or county and state. Intervals 1-11 (1 = Jan-Feb ... 11 = Nov-Dec) or RMA's codes 625-635; default all 11. source ncei (default, current data) or cpc (previous data). coverage_level 70-90 adds whether each year pays (index below the coverage level) and its payment factor. Hawaii IDs such as "H0319" have indexes but no precipitation or average. RMA's Actuarial Information Browser is the authority for actual indemnities. Example: {"grid_ids": [26516], "years": {"start": 2016, "end": 2025}, "intervals": [629], "coverage_level": 85}

tools.name: noaa_compare_sources
tools.description: How does the switch from CPC (previous data) to NCEI (current data) change these grids' PRF index and payouts? Use for whether the switch helped or hurt, or which years would have paid differently; use noaa_get_grid_index for one source's yearly values. Compares RMA's newest CPC and NCEI index files over the years both cover, not live precipitation. Per grid and interval: the mean index shift (NCEI minus CPC, percentage points), the correlation, and the years that pay under one source only, newest first, with both indexes and the coverage levels (70, 75, 80, 85, 90) where it differs (the newest 5 and a count of the rest; detail "years" lists them all); per grid, payouts gained and lost under NCEI at 90% and the interval with the biggest shift. Place: grid_ids (1-20), latitude and longitude (neighbors adds the grids around), or county and state. Intervals 1-11 (1 = Jan-Feb ... 11 = Nov-Dec) or RMA's codes 625-635; default all 11. years: {start, end} or a count of the newest; default every shared year. Hawaii IDs such as "H0319" are supported. RMA's Actuarial Information Browser is the authority for actual indemnities. Example: {"grid_ids": [26516], "intervals": [629, 630]}

tools.name: noaa_get_basis_risk
tools.description: How well does the grid index match my spot? Scores each subgrid (1/24-degree cell) of the grid against the grid's PRF index over past years: the missed rate (subgrid dry, own index below the coverage level, while the grid didn't pay), the windfall rate (grid paid while the subgrid wasn't dry), the correlation between the grid's index and each subgrid's (median and worst subgrid), and the intervals with the most risk, ranked. NCEI only. Use noaa_get_subgrid_precipitation for where precipitation fell recently, noaa_get_grid_index for the grid's yearly indexes. Place: grid_ids (1-5), latitude and longitude, or county and state (at most 5 grids). interval: one of 1-11 (1 = Jan-Feb ... 11 = Nov-Dec) or RMA's code 625-635; default all 11, ranked. sub_id: one subgrid of a single grid (noaa_find_grid gives it for a point). years: {start, end} or a count of the newest, at most 35; default 1991 through the latest year in RMA's NCEI file. coverage_level 70-90, default 90. detail "years" adds each year's grid index and the subgrids missed or paid without being dry. Subgrid precipitation is fetched from NCEI for the scored years and cached, so a first call can take a while. The gauge badge says how many gauges stand behind the subgrids; SPARSE or unknown means the subgrid detail is unreliable. Example: {"grid_ids": [26516], "interval": 629, "coverage_level": 85}

instructions:
NOAA precipitation and the USDA RMA Rainfall Index (PRF) for 0.25-degree grids.
Place: every tool but noaa_get_data_status takes exactly one of grid_ids, latitude and longitude (neighbors: true adds the up to 8 grids around), or county and state, and answers for the grids it resolves to. A city or address goes in as its coordinates; noaa_find_grid shows the grids and counties for a place.
Now by default, history on request: a bare question gets the current picture against the average. Give years only when the user asks about past years.
Which tool: will my policy pay this crop year (or get rained out) = noaa_policy_outlook; how this coverage would have done in past years = noaa_policy_history; the interval in progress, day by day = noaa_track_interval; how much precipitation = noaa_get_precipitation; where inside a grid it fell = noaa_get_subgrid_precipitation; each year's index = noaa_get_grid_index; old vs new data, or whether the switch helped or hurt = noaa_compare_sources; how well the grid index matches a spot = noaa_get_basis_risk; which grids are at a place = noaa_find_grid; how current the data is = noaa_get_data_status.
Data: NCEI is the current data RMA uses for PRF from crop year 2027; CPC is the previous data. Old or previous = CPC; new or current = NCEI. Tools default to NCEI; noaa_get_precipitation and noaa_get_grid_index take source "cpc", and noaa_get_precipitation also "both"; noaa_compare_sources always reads both. The policy tools cover NCEI crop years (2027 on) only.
PRF: intervals 1-11 (1 = Jan-Feb ... 11 = Nov-Dec) or RMA's codes 625-635. Coverage levels 70, 75, 80, 85, 90. A grid pays when its index (precipitation as % of the interval's average) is below the coverage level.
Index labels: published (RMA's final index, what RMA pays on), final (computed RMA's way from NCEI's final months, before RMA publishes), estimate (a month still preliminary). For other values only stage final is final.
Say "precipitation", not rain or rainfall, except in RMA's product name "Rainfall Index" and "rained out". RMA's Actuarial Information Browser is the authority for actual indemnities.
